_comment: __text baseline for the binary-size CI gate (see check_gate.py and .github/workflows/binary_size.yml). Measured osx-arm64, 2026-08-05. Regenerate after an intentional size change with: pixi run -e dev python3 benchmarks/binary_size/check_gate.py --update Last raised 2026-08-05 by M1.0, which widened comparison dispatch from NumericType to PrimitiveType: query_streaming +0.512%, query_join +1.154%. That is the cost of emitting comparison leaves for temporal, interval and decimal -- i.e. of supporting those dtypes at all -- and it buys row-group pruning on date and decimal predicates, which ClickBench needs. Lowered dramatically 2026-08-05 by Q4.7: hashing decoded dictionary keys via `cast`, which made all of `kernels.cast` reachable from every binary that hashes. Decoding by `take` instead removed ~2.4 MB from each -- query_join -63.5%, agg_fused -64.6%, agg -55.3%. Reset 2026-08-17 on the post-fix tree, and the history matters because the gate was red by 42-96% at the time, not by the +0.449% recorded at the time. Investigating before resetting attributed nearly all of it to one commit: f5226d5 ("migrate closures to the unified value-taking form") added +739,316 bytes (+54.8%) to query_streaming_agg_fused, while its own commit message and CHANGELOG entry claimed "Binary size max +0.36%". A single-variable A/B settles it -- f5226d5 and its parent 5435f59 build with the identical pinned toolchain and measure 2,089,084 vs 1,349,768. The Mojo 1.1 / MAX 26.6 upgrade accounted for only +0.39%, and GPU gating was intact (-D MARROW_GPU=true still costs +308,008, and no device symbols reach a default build). The cause was the interposed `narrow` closure layer in the shared variant_dispatch helper, whose DynArray-returning instantiations were 55.9% of __text; removing it recovered 662,740 bytes (89.6%) and roughly halved cold build times. Old -> new here: query_streaming 1,332,456 -> 1,484,652 (+11.4%), query_join 1,410,788 -> 1,507,836 (+6.9%), query_streaming_agg_fused 1,338,468 -> 1,417,476 (+5.9%), query_streaming_agg 1,858,644 -> 1,932,404 (+4.0%). That residue is ~600 commits of legitimate work plus V0's measured +0.136% (ListScalar carrying its own dtype, so a map element reports map<...> rather than list<struct<...>>). threshold_pct stays 0.5 -- it is what caught this, and it is not raised. The real lesson is not the reset: a +55% regression survived ten commits because this gate is not in CI and CI has not run since 2026-05-11. Added query_dynvalue 2026-08-18 (S4/A1): the four gates above link *zero* symbols from marrow.kernels.cast -- checked with `nm -C` on all eleven benchmark binaries -- so the entire cast family was ungated, and a change that added +435,072 bytes (+7.09%) to query_dynvalue measured 0.00% on every gate the CI actually watches. query_dynvalue links 693 cast symbols (query_runtime and query_sort also link the ladder and are still ungated; one gate was judged enough signal for the cost of the extra sweep time). Its baseline is recorded at 4,871,156, which is 1,268,480 bytes BELOW the 6,139,636 measured at 8cc9723: splitting DecimalCast's single _convert[FromN, ToN] -- monomorphized over the full decimal-union-numeric cross product on both sides -- into five per-conversion kernels narrowed each one's dispatch to the families it can actually see. The lesson is the gate gap, not the win: 1,476 bytes of added source cost 371,584 bytes of __text through that cross product, a 250x multiplier that nothing would have reported. Added query_expr2_streaming and query_expr2_agg_fused 2026-08-23 (plan Tier 1.1): before them, not one of the five gates built anything from marrow/expr2/, so `pixi run binary_size` reported ~0.00% no matter what the expression rewrite did and every size claim about that work was unfalsifiable. Recorded at 1,358,480 and 1,320,356 on the tree that added expr2's Aggregate relation. They are NOT comparable to their expr/ twins: expr2's comptime Column[T] is bound on NumericType, so both gates use int64 where query_streaming and query_streaming_agg_fused use a string column. Their job is to catch expr2 regressing against itself -- in particular the to_processor() symmetry refactor, whose cost is otherwise a guess. Re-recorded 2026-08-29 on osx-arm64 after the `exprold` deletion and the aggregate rearchitecture. This was a deliberate re-record, not a side effect: five of the seven gates now build a materially different program, so the previous floor could not distinguish a regression from the port. `query_streaming_agg` moved 1,932,404 -> 9,940,868 because it went from an `exprold` plan to a runtime-lane `expr` plan carrying the whole name-resolution ladder; that is a different program, not a 5x regression. Known and accepted at this floor: the aggregate gates carry ~+18.7 KB that three single-variable A/Bs could not attribute. Re-recorded 2026-08-30 after the Python query API was restored. Two separate movements are folded in and they must not be confused. (1) The five *fused* gates each fell 0.44-0.53% -- query_streaming 1,483,336 -> 1,476,580, query_join 1,641,324 -> 1,633,200, query_streaming_agg_fused 1,481,012 -> 1,473,136, query_expr2_streaming 1,473,192 -> 1,466,724, query_expr2_agg_fused 1,479,612 -> 1,472,240. That is the Mojo 1.1.0.dev2026083005 / MAX 26.6.0.dev2026083005 upgrade (bb1a305f), not this change: no comptime-lane source moved. (2) The two *runtime* gates grew hard -- query_dynvalue 6,227,524 -> 8,460,880 (+35.9%) and query_streaming_agg 9,940,868 -> 12,020,880 (+20.9%). That is the cost of giving the runtime lane the ~45 verbs the comptime lane already had (arithmetic, math, strings, temporal, null predicates, cast, isin, array_length), each a new tag in RuntimeValue.evaluate. The interpreter is one function that names every kernel it can dispatch to, so a binary reaching the lane at all links all of them. This is the trade CLAUDE.md sanctions and the symbol table confirms the scoping exactly: `marrow::expr::runtime` is 0 symbols in every gate except the three that build runtime values, so no AOT binary pays for it. Do not read the +36% as a regression to chase -- read it as the runtime lane's floor, and gate future changes against *this* number. Raised once more in the same session by the `StructArray.field` slice fix: `field` now carries the struct's offset/length down to the child, and that call inlines into every column leaf. It costs +5,632 b on each fused gate (query_streaming 1,476,580 -> 1,484,132, +0.511%, which is what tripped the 0.5% threshold; streaming_agg_fused, expr2_streaming and expr2_agg_fused all +0.38%), +4,096 b on query_streaming_agg, +2,112 b on query_dynvalue, and +0 on query_join. That is the price of a correctness fix, not a regression: without it a sliced struct handed every reader the parent's full column, which the comptime lane turned into a silent wrong answer at offset > 0. See `test_struct_array_field_carries_the_slice`. Added query_cli 2026-08-31 with QueryCli, the AOT lane's command-line surface. Recorded at 2,965,016 -- against query_scan's 2,633,844 and query_param's 2,745,760 measured in the same sweep, so the CLI layer (argparse, both renderers, the parameter coercion and the format dispatch) is +331,172 over a bare Parquet scan and +219,256 over the same query binding its parameter by hand. What it gates is the property, not the number: `marrow::expr::runtime` is 0 symbols and so are `marrow::parquet::writer` and `marrow::ipc`, because `run()` takes its writers as comptime parameters and this gate does not name them. A single-variable A/B confirmed the `from .cli import ...` re-export in `marrow/expr/__init__.mojo` costs exactly 0: query_streaming measured 1,523,716 with and without it, byte for byte. NOTE: the six pre-existing gate numbers below were recorded at a27167aa and are stale by 12 commits of optimizer work -- query_streaming measures 1,523,716 here against the 1,484,132 recorded (+2.67%), and that delta predates query_cli, which did not exist at a27167aa. Whoever lands the optimizer branch should re-record; query_cli's own number is measured on this tree and is not affected.
